tts: A fitness influencer sold her brand for one point eight billion dollars. Meanwhile, a million views pays way less than you'd think. So where does the money really come from?

First, why are there suddenly so many of them? Fitness is perfect content: a new workout every day, and the most powerful format on the internet, before and after. Then the pandemic closed the gyms, and millions of people started working out at home, from videos.
But here's the first surprise: views pay pennies. That's why almost every video has a promo code. An influencer recommends a protein powder and gets a cut of every purchase you make.
Next, their own programs. A workout is filmed once and sold thousands of times. That's almost pure profit.
And at the top, their own brand. Katy Hearn started out posting workouts, and in twenty twenty-five her energy drink brand sold for one point eight billion.
Kayla Itsines sold her workout app for hundreds of millions, and two years later bought it back for a fraction of that.
But here's what nobody tells you. Only about four percent of creators make over a hundred thousand dollars a year. Most make almost nothing. You just never see them.
So a fitness influencer isn't selling you workouts. They're selling trust. And you pay for it, one promo code at a time.
